Badge.keyNotes:
Badge.kt has ZERO dependencies on other unported miuix components — it imports ONLY theme (LocalContentColor, LocalTextStyles, MiuixTheme). Colors error/onError and textStyle footnote2 are all already present. Safe to port immediately; it unblocks NavigationBar/NavigationRail (they call the internal badgeBounds()/rulers). Exposes two widgets + a defaults class.

EXACT CONSTANTS (dp = logical px, verbatim):
- BadgeDefaults.Size = 6 (icon-only "dot" badge min size)
- BadgeDefaults.LargeSize = 16 (min size when content present)
- containerColor = colors.error ; contentColor = colors.onError
- shape = CircleShape → use StadiumBorder (fully-rounded pill). A 6x6 dot renders as a circle; a content pill has fully-rounded ends. Do NOT use a fixed cornerRadius.
- BadgeWithContentHorizontalPadding = 4 (EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal:4), applied ONLY when content != null)
- BadgeWithContentHorizontalOffset = 12 ; BadgeWithContentVerticalOffset = 14 (offsets used when badge HAS content)
- BadgeOffset = 6 (offset used on BOTH axes when NO content)

MiuixBadge widget:
- size = content != null ? 16 : 6.
- Structure: Row (verticalAlignment center, horizontalArrangement center) with ConstrainedBox(minWidth:size, minHeight:size) + ShapeDecoration(color: containerColor, shape: StadiumBorder()). Add horizontal:4 padding only when content != null. Content is caller-provided Widget? (default null → empty dot).
- content styling is the ONE subtle part. Source wraps content in ProvideContentColorTextStyle: it (a) provides contentColor as LocalContentColor, and (b) MERGES footnote2 (11sp) into LocalTextStyles.main, then further copies lineHeight=16.sp + LineHeightStyle(alignment=Center, trim=None). Because our ported MiuixText reads MiuixTheme.of(context).textStyles.main (NOT DefaultTextStyle) and resolves color = color ?? base.color ?? MiuixContentColor.of(context), the faithful reproduction is: wrap content in MiuixContentColor(color: contentColor, child: MiuixTheme(data: theme.copyWith(textStyles: theme.textStyles.copy(main: theme.textStyles.main.merge(theme.textStyles.footnote2).copyWith(height: 16/11, leadingDistribution: TextLeadingDistribution.even))), child: content)). The merge yields fontSize 11; height:16/11 (~1.4545) reproduces the 16sp line box; leadingDistribution.even reproduces LineHeightStyle center alignment (extra leading split evenly above/below to vertically center the digits). Wrapping DefaultTextStyle alone will NOT work because MiuixText ignores it — must override the MiuixTheme textStyles.main.

MiuixBadgedBox layout (custom measure): use CustomMultiChildLayout + MultiChildLayoutDelegate with two LayoutId children "anchor" and "badge".
- anchor child = content wrapped in a centered Box (Alignment.center); badge child = the badge.
- Measure anchor with incoming constraints; the overall widget size = anchor size (width x height). Measure badge with LOOSE height (BoxConstraints.loose or minHeight:0) so text isn't stretched.
- hasContent = badgeSize.width > 6 (compares measured badge width against BadgeDefaults.Size). Empty Badge() measures 6 wide → false; content badge ≥16 → true. This inference exactly mirrors the source.
- hOffset = hasContent ? 12 : 6 ; vOffset = hasContent ? 14 : 6.
- Place anchor at (0,0). Default (standalone, no ruler bounds) placement: badgeX = anchorWidth - hOffset ; badgeY = vOffset - badgeHeight. Concretely: content badge (h=16) → badgeY = 14-16 = -2 (hangs 2px above anchor top, right edge inset 12px from anchor right); dot badge (h=6) → badgeY = 6-6 = 0 (flush top, inset 6px). Badge is positioned top-END corner of the anchor.
- Source clamps with rulers: badgeX = min(anchorW - hOffset, endRuler - badgeW); badgeY = max(vOffset - badgeH, topRuler). With no rulers provided endRuler=+INF and topRuler=-INF, so clamping is a no-op → the default formulas above are EXACT for standalone use. NavigationBar/Rail apply badgeBounds() which sets endRuler=itemWidth, topRuler=0 to keep the badge inside the item. Port the unbounded default now; optionally expose an optional clamp param (endBound/topBound doubles, default null=unbounded) so Nav components can pass item bounds later — do NOT try to replicate the Compose Ruler API.
- placeRelative is RTL-aware (mirrors X). For 1:1 you may read Directionality and mirror when RTL; app is mobile — a simple LTR top-right placement is acceptable if RTL isn't used, but note it.
- The source also republishes anchor-only FirstBaseline/LastBaseline as the widget's baselines; Flutter baseline propagation differs and this only matters if a parent baseline-aligns the BadgedBox — safe to skip (note as a minor fidelity gap).

Defaults class per conventions: class MiuixBadgeDefaults { MiuixBadgeDefaults._(); static const double size = 6; static const double largeSize = 16; static Color containerColor(BuildContext c) => MiuixTheme.of(c).colors.error; static Color contentColor(BuildContext c) => MiuixTheme.of(c).colors.onError; } Also keep internal consts (badgeWithContentHorizontalPadding=4, offsets 12/14/6) private in the file.
Badge.name: Badge
Badge.platformConcerns: Compose HorizontalRuler/VerticalRuler (BadgeTopRuler/BadgeEndRuler + Modifier.badgeBounds) is a Compose 1.7 layout feature with no Flutter equivalent. It only clamps the badge inside NavigationBar/NavigationRail item bounds; for a standalone BadgedBox the rulers are +INF/-INF so clamping is a no-op. Closest Flutter approach: implement the unbounded default placement via CustomMultiChildLayout now, and expose an optional (endBound/topBound) clamp param that Nav components can supply once ported — instead of reimplementing rulers. Second concern: LineHeightStyle(alignment=Center) for vertically centering the single-line label → reproduce with TextStyle.height=16/11 plus TextLeadingDistribution.even (baked into the theme-override main style, since MiuixText doesn't accept a leadingDistribution arg). Third: FirstBaseline/LastBaseline alignment-line republication doesn't map to Flutter's baseline model; drop it (only affects a baseline-aligning parent, not present here).

Scaffold.keyNotes:
DEPENDENCY REALITY: Only hard unported dep is MiuixPopupUtils. Scaffold's default `popupHost = { MiuixPopupHost() }` and it wires 4 composition locals: LocalPopupStates, LocalDialogStates, LocalRootDialogStates, LocalRootPopupStates (defined in utils/MiuixPopupUtils.kt lines 595-598). Root-state logic: `rootDialogStates = LocalRootDialogStates.current ?: dialogStates` and `rootPopupStates = LocalRootPopupStates.current ?: popupStates` — a nested Scaffold reuses the ancestor's root state lists; a top-level Scaffold becomes the root. Port these as InheritedWidgets with a maybe-of null-check. `popupStates`/`dialogStates` are per-Scaffold `mutableStateListOf` — model as a small state object (e.g. lists held in a State). If MiuixPopupUtils isn't ported yet, the port can temporarily accept an optional `popupHost` widget defaulting to SizedBox.shrink() and stub the 4 providers, but do NOT ship that as final. OverlayDialog is only in doc comments — not a code dep. All slot params (topBar/bottomBar/fab/toolbar/snackbar) are caller-supplied builders, NOT build-order blockers.

COLORS/STYLES: containerColor default = MiuixTheme.of(context).colors.surface. Surface wrapper supplies onSurface as content color (already handled by MiuixSurface). No text styles, no new tokens.

CONSTANTS (verbatim): FabSpacing = 12.dp; FloatingToolbarSpacing = 4.dp. FabPosition values Start=0,Center=1,End=2,EndOverlay=3. ToolbarPosition values TopStart=0,CenterStart=1,BottomStart=2,TopEnd=3,CenterEnd=4,BottomEnd=5,TopCenter=6,BottomCenter=7. Default floatingActionButtonPosition = End; default floatingToolbarPosition = BottomCenter.

LAYOUT ENGINE: Kotlin uses SubcomposeLayout so it can measure topBar/bottomBar, compute a contentPadding, THEN subcompose body with that padding. Flutter has no subcompose-after-measure. Faithful approach: CustomMultiChildLayout + MultiChildLayoutDelegate is not enough alone because the body BUILDER needs bar heights at build time. Recommended: keep a `ValueNotifier<EdgeInsets> _contentPadding` (mirrors miuix's single mutable `paddingHolder` PaddingValues that updates during measure without recomposing the whole scaffold); a custom layout/RenderBox writes bar heights into it during layout; wrap the body in `ValueListenableBuilder<EdgeInsets>` so only the content rebuilds when padding changes (one-frame settle, imperceptible; typically stable after first frame). Body is measured/placed at full size (0,0) with loose constraints — it fills the whole scaffold; the CONTENT applies the padding itself (like extendBody + extendBodyBehindAppBar always true). content signature = `Widget Function(EdgeInsets contentPadding)`.

contentPadding computation: top = topBar present ? topBarHeight : insets.top; bottom = bottomBar present ? bottomBarHeight : insets.bottom; start = insets.left; end = insets.right. "present" = placeable width==0 && height==0 → empty. Insets come from contentWindowInsets.asPaddingValues.

WINDOW INSETS: default contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.union(WindowInsets.displayCutout) → Flutter `MediaQuery.paddingOf(context)`. topInset/leftInset/rightInset/bottomInset are read as pixels. `onConsumedWindowInsetsChanged { safeInsets = contentWindowInsets.exclude(consumed) }` → Flutter's MediaQuery.padding is already reduced by ancestor SafeArea/MediaQuery.removePadding, so reading MediaQuery.paddingOf gives the equivalent excluded value; nested scaffolds under a SafeArea naturally get reduced padding. Note this mapping in a comment.

MEASUREMENT CONSTRAINTS: snackbar, fab, floatingToolbar are each measured with looseConstraints.offset(-leftInset-rightInset, -bottomInset) (available minus horizontal insets and bottom inset). topBar, bottomBar, body, popup use full loose constraints.

PLACEMENT / DRAW ORDER (bottom→top): 1) body at (0,0); 2) topBar at (0,0); 3) snackbar; 4) bottomBar at (0, layoutHeight - bottomBarHeight); 5) floatingToolbar; 6) fab; 7) popup at (0,0) topmost. (Measurement order differs — popup is measured first — but this is the paint/Stack order.)

FAB horizontal offset (RTL-aware): Start → LTR: FabSpacing+leftInset ; RTL: layoutWidth-FabSpacing-fabWidth-rightInset. End/EndOverlay → LTR: layoutWidth-FabSpacing-fabWidth-rightInset ; RTL: FabSpacing+leftInset. Center(else) → (layoutWidth-fabWidth+leftInset-rightInset)/2.
FAB vertical: fabOffsetFromBottom = (bottomBar empty || position==EndOverlay) ? fabHeight+FabSpacing+bottomInset : bottomBarHeight+fabHeight+FabSpacing. FAB placed at (fabLeftOffset, layoutHeight-fabOffsetFromBottom). If fab empty, skip.

SNACKBAR: snackbarOffsetFromBottom = snackbarHeight==0 ? 0 : snackbarHeight + (fabOffsetFromBottom ?? (bottomBar present ? bottomBarHeight : null) ?? bottomInset). Placed at x=(layoutWidth-snackbarWidth+leftInset-rightInset)/2, y=layoutHeight-snackbarOffsetFromBottom.

FLOATING TOOLBAR: availableWidth = layoutWidth-leftInset-rightInset; availableHeight = layoutHeight-topBarHeight-topInset-bottomInset. Use position.toAlignment() to align a box of (toolbarWidth,toolbarHeight) inside (availableWidth,availableHeight) respecting layoutDirection (Alignment.align → in Flutter compute via Alignment.inscribe or manual: x = align.x fraction over free width, etc.). Final x = leftInset + alignedX; y = topBarHeight + topInset + alignedY - FloatingToolbarSpacing (note the -4.dp lift). Skip if toolbar empty.

RTL: honor Directionality.of(context) for start/end padding and FAB Start/End resolution. The Alignment.vertical/horizontal helper extensions in the file are unused by the placement path (only toAlignment is) — you can skip porting them.

FLUTTER MECHANISM: Best to implement as a dedicated RenderBox (extends RenderBox with slotted children) or a StatefulWidget wrapping a custom MultiChildRenderObjectWidget to replicate measure-then-feed-padding; a simpler CustomMultiChildLayout works if paired with the ValueNotifier+ValueListenableBuilder body-rebuild trick above. Surface wrapper → MiuixSurface(color: containerColor, child: ...). Provide FabPlacement as a private helper class (left,width,height).
Scaffold.name: Scaffold
Scaffold.platformConcerns: Window insets: WindowInsets.systemBars.union(displayCutout) → MediaQuery.paddingOf(context); the onConsumedWindowInsetsChanged/exclude(consumed) behavior maps to MediaQuery.padding already being reduced by ancestor SafeArea/MediaQuery.removePadding (no direct equivalent to per-layout consumed-inset callback, but the MediaQuery reduction achieves the same nested-scaffold result). SubcomposeLayout (measure bars, then subcompose body with computed padding) has no Flutter analog — closest is a custom RenderObject or CustomMultiChildLayout writing bar heights into a ValueNotifier<EdgeInsets> and rebuilding only the body via ValueListenableBuilder (one-frame settle). RTL layoutDirection → Directionality.of(context). Nested/root popup+dialog state propagation (LocalRoot*States ?: local) → InheritedWidget with maybeOf null-fallback. No blur/sensor/haptic concerns in this file.

Dropdown.keyNotes:
SCOPE: This file (Dropdown.kt) contains ONLY the option-row renderer + data models + colors/defaults. It does NOT contain the popup trigger, the popup container, submenu cascading, or any overlay logic — those live in separate files (ListPopup / SuperDropdown / MiuixPopupUtils, to be ported later). So this port has ZERO unported-component deps and can be built immediately. `children`/`onClick`/`hasSubmenu` are just data fields consumed by the future cascading layer; here `hasSubmenu` only switches the trailing icon (chevron vs check) and semantics role.

NO SQUIRCLE, NO ANIMATION, NO SPRING in this file. Background is a plain solid rect (Compose `drawBehind { drawRect(bg) }`) — use a ColoredBox / DecoratedBox with a rectangular (un-rounded) fill. No press feedback ripple is configured (rows draw their own bg); use GestureDetector(onTap) gated by `enabled`, NOT MiuixPressable, to match. Wrap in Semantics(selected: isSelected, button: hasSubmenu, inMutuallyExclusiveGroup/ radio: !hasSubmenu).

EXACT DEFAULTS (DropdownDefaults, all dp = logical px):
- MinHeight = 56 (dialog mode min row height)
- MinWidth = 200 (dialog mode min row width)
- CheckIconSize = 20 (trailing check drawn at 20x20)
- ArrowSize = 10 x 16 (up-down arrow in ArrowEndAction)
- ChevronSize = 10 x 16 (submenu chevron)
- IconMinSize = 26 (leading icon cell min width & height)
- MaxItemTextWidth = 216 (popup-mode max width of inner icon+text row)
- InsideHorizontalPadding = 20 (row horizontal padding, popup mode)
- DialogHorizontalPadding = 28 (row horizontal padding, dialog mode)
- FirstLastVerticalPadding = 20 (top pad on first row / bottom pad on last row, popup mode only)
- MiddleVerticalPadding = 12 (top/bottom pad for middle rows in popup; ALL rows top/bottom in dialog mode)
- IconEndPadding = 12 (gap after leading icon cell)
- CheckIconStartPadding = 12 (gap before trailing check/chevron)

LAYOUT (outer Row: verticalAlignment=center, horizontalArrangement=SpaceBetween):
- Container modifier: dialog mode = ConstrainedBox(minHeight:56, minWidth:200) + fill available width + EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal:28); popup mode = EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal:20). Then add EdgeInsets.only(top: additionalTop, bottom: additionalBottom).
- additionalTop = (!dialogMode && isFirst) ? 20 : 12 ; additionalBottom = (!dialogMode && isLast) ? 20 : 12. In dialog mode both are always 12. Defaults: isFirst = index==0, isLast = index==optionSize-1.
- IMPORTANT SpaceBetween nuance: popup mode outer Row is wrap-content (no fillMaxWidth) → use MainAxisSize.min so SpaceBetween is inert and the trailing icon simply follows the text with its 12 start-padding. Dialog mode uses full width → MainAxisSize.max so the trailing icon is pushed to the trailing edge.
- Inner row (icon+text, Start arrangement, center vertical): popup mode wrap it in ConstrainedBox(maxWidth:216); dialog mode no width limit.
  - Leading icon cell (if item.icon!=null): ConstrainedBox(minWidth:26, minHeight:26) + Padding(right:12). item.icon is a caller-supplied widget (Kotlin @Composable (Modifier)->Unit → Dart Widget?).
  - Column: title Text(fontSize = textStyles.body1.fontSize, fontWeight = FontWeight.w500 (Medium), color = titleColor); if summary!=null a second Text(fontSize = textStyles.body2.fontSize, default weight, color = summaryColor). Use MiuixText.
- Trailing icon (with Padding(left:12)): if hasSubmenu → ArrowRight chevron sized 10x16; else → Check sized 20x20 (padding+size = CheckIconBaseModifier / ChevronIconBaseModifier).

PullToRefresh.keyNotes:
NO theme tokens used — color is hardcoded Compose Color.Gray = Color(0xFF888888); refreshTextStyle is built inline (fontSize 14, FontWeight.bold, color=gray). No colorScheme/textStyles references at all.

DEFAULTS: refreshThreshold=0.25 (clamped 0..1); circleSize=20; color=0xFF888888; refreshTexts=["Pull down to refresh","Release to refresh","Refreshing...","Refreshed successfully"]; refreshTextStyle=TextStyle(fontSize:14, fontWeight:bold, color:gray). Constants MAX_DRAWRATIO=1/6, THRESHOLD_RADIO=1/4.

PIXEL/DP: Compose mixes px (via density) and dp. In Flutter EVERYTHING is logical px — drop all toPx/toDp; use container height directly. containerHeight H = MediaQuery/LayoutBuilder constraints.maxHeight. Derived (verbatim): maxDragDistance=H; fullDragRange=obtainDampingDistance(1,H)=H/3; refreshThresholdOffset=H*(1/6)*(1/4)=H/24 (fixed visual threshold); triggerProgressOffset=refreshThreshold*fullDragRange=0.25*H/3=H/12; effectiveThresholdOffset=max(H/24,H/12)=H/12 (denominator of pullProgress); visualProgress denominator scaleEndOffset=min(H/24,H/12)=H/24 (so scale-up completes at the SMALLER threshold). pullProgress=(dragOffset/effectiveThreshold).clamp(0,1); fullDragProgress=(dragOffset/fullDragRange).clamp(0,1); visualProgress=(dragOffset/scaleEnd).clamp(0,1).

DAMPING MATH (port verbatim from SpringUtils.kt): obtainDampingDistance(n,range): x=n.clamp(0,1); factor=x - x^2 + x^3/3; return factor*range. obtainTouchDistance(px,range): abs=|px| clamped to obtainDampingDistance(1,range); base=range-3*abs; return range - range^(2/3)*sign(base)*|base|^(1/3). Drag apply loop (onPost/PreScroll): currentTouch+=delta, clamp(-H,H); normalized=min(|currentTouch|/H,1); dragOffset=sign(currentTouch)*obtainDampingDistance(normalized,H). State from dragOffset: >=triggerProgressOffset→ThresholdReached; >0→Pulling; else Idle.

SPRING: SpringEngine = critical damping ratio 1.0, naturalPeriod 0.4s standard (0.55s only if |initialVel|>5000 — never hit here, all animateToSpring calls start vel=0). Euler integrate: ω=2π/period, k/m=ω², c/m=2*ζ*ω; v = v*(1-c/m*dt)+k/m*(target-pos)*dt; pos+=dt*v; dt clamped [0.001,0.016]; settle when |pos-target|<1.0. FAITHFUL FLUTTER: AnimationController.unbounded(vsync).animateWith(SpringSimulation(folmeSpring(damping:1.0,response:0.4), start,target,0)) — same pattern as miuix_top_app_bar _SpringSimulation. Each animation frame you MUST also update currentTouch=obtainTouchDistance(dragOffset,H) so a mid-flight catch stays visually consistent. animateToSpring cancels any prior job first. For pixel-exact fidelity you may instead port the Euler loop with a Ticker, but folmeSpring is acceptable.

STATE MACHINE (5 states) + hoisted two-way isRefreshing sync: (1) rising edge isRefreshing=true while Idle → showRefreshing: set Refreshing, animateToSpring(H/24), then a while-loop re-chases the target if H/24 moved (covers first-frame H unknown). (2) isRefreshing=false while Refreshing → finishRefreshing: cancel anim job, set RefreshComplete, run completion anim. (3) pointer release (Pulling/ThresholdReached + all pointers up) → handlePointerRelease: if dragOffset>=triggerProgressOffset → startRefreshing (spring to H/24, then Refreshing + fire onRefresh only if not already refreshing), else rebound animateToSpring(0)→resetToIdle. Guards isProcessingRelease/isTouching/isRebounding must be replicated. Completion anim (startManualRefreshCompleteAnimation): Animatable initial=1-(dragOffset/H24).clamp(0,1); tween 200ms Cubic(0,0,0,0.37) to 1; each frame dragOffset=H24*(1-value), then set Idle. onRefresh must be called AFTER internalRefreshState=Refreshing (ordering guards the lost-pulse latch). Pointer-release detection: Compose awaitPointerEvent → Flutter Listener(onPointerUp/onPointerCancel).

LAYOUT: Box>Column[ RefreshHeader (offset y = contentPadding.top), content() ]. Header pushes content down as it grows (both in Column). RefreshHeader = Column(fillMaxWidth, height=headerHeight, CenterHorizontally, top): [RefreshIndicator height=indicatorHeight, Text(top padding 6, alpha=refreshTextAlpha)]. stretchExtra = dragOffset - H/24 (negative during scale phase). indicatorHeight: Idle→0; stretchExtra<=0 → circleSize*visualProgress; else circleSize+stretchExtra. headerHeight: Idle→0; stretchExtra<=0 → (circleSize+36)*visualProgress; else (circleSize+36)+stretchExtra.

TEXT per state: Idle""; Pulling→texts[0] only if visualProgress>0.5; ThresholdReached→texts[1]; Refreshing→texts[2]; RefreshComplete→texts[3]. refreshTextAlpha: Idle 0; Pulling (progress>0.6 ? (progress-0.5)*2 : 0); ThresholdReached 1; Refreshing ((visualProgress-0.5)*2).clamp(0,1); RefreshComplete (1 - completeProgress*1.95).clamp(min 0).

CANVAS (size=circleSize=20 box, TopCenter): ringStrokeWidth=circleSize/11≈1.818; radius=max(size.minDimension/2, circleSize/3.5)=max(10,5.71)=10; center=Offset(circleSize/2=10, circleSize/1.8≈11.11). Draw modes: Pulling & dragOffset<=threshold → drawCircle(stroke round, alpha=(visualProgress-0.2).clamp(min0)). Pulling/ThresholdReached & dragOffset>threshold → drawThresholdIndicator: capsule = arc(180°,sweep180 top-half at center.y) + arc(0°,sweep180 bottom-half at center.y+lineLength) + two vertical lines at x=center.x±radius from topY to bottomY; lineLength=(dragOffset-threshold).clamp(0, maxDrag-threshold); all Stroke round. Refreshing → drawCircle full ring + orbiting dot: orbitRadius=radius-2*strokeWidth≈6.36, angle=rotation*π/180, dot at center+(orbit*cos,orbit*sin), dot filled radius=strokeWidth; ring color premultiplied by expansionAlpha=((visualProgress-0.2)/0.8).clamp(0,1). RefreshComplete → drawCircle stroke, animatedRadius=radius*(1-progress).clamp(min 0.9), alpha=(1-progress-0.35).clamp(min0), y=center.y-radius-strokeWidth+animatedRadius.

ROTATION: only while Refreshing. infiniteRepeatable tween 800ms LinearEasing, Restart, initialValue=random(0..360), sweeps +360. Flutter: AnimationController(duration:800ms)..repeat(), Curves.linear, add random start offset.

HAPTIC: on entering ThresholdReached → HapticFeedbackType.GestureThresholdActivate → Flutter HapticFeedback.selectionClick() (closest; or lightImpact).

PullToRefresh.platformConcerns:
BIGGEST ISSUE — NestedScrollConnection has NO Flutter equivalent. Compose intercepts and CONSUMES scroll deltas via onPreScroll/onPostScroll/onPreFling/onPostFling and negotiates a chain (TopAppBar behavior first when Idle, refresh first otherwise; Refreshing/RefreshComplete consume ALL scroll). Flutter's NotificationListener<ScrollNotification> is OBSERVE-ONLY (cannot consume). Recommended faithful port (mirrors Flutter's own RefreshIndicator): NotificationListener + OverscrollNotification (overscroll.overscroll<0 at top = pull-down → feed |delta| into currentTouch/applyDrag) + ScrollUpdateNotification + ScrollStartNotification, driving the growing header (which naturally displaces content, matching miuix's Column layout). Use ClampingScrollPhysics on the inner list so the top-edge pull is available as overscroll. To 'consume upward drag to hide the indicator' when dragOffset>0 (Compose onPreScroll available.y<0 path), gate with an active pull flag and, while dragOffset>0, absorb ScrollUpdate deltas into applyDrag before the list scrolls (may require a custom ScrollPhysics or intercepting via a Listener on pointer moves). Pointer-up detection → Listener(onPointerUp/onPointerCancel) since NotificationListener has no reliable release event.

MiuixPopupUtils.keyNotes:
FOUNDATIONAL — port this FIRST; it is the overlay/dialog/popup infra that Scaffold, Dialog, Popup, BottomSheet, ListPopup, Dropdown, Tooltip, Snackbar all depend on. It depends on NO other unported component (Scaffold/OverlayDialog imports are KDoc-only). Only color token used: colorScheme.windowDimming (already in list; has built-in alpha). No text styles.

ARCHITECTURE: In Compose, DialogLayout/PopupLayout render nothing — they REGISTER a state object into a global mutableStateListOf (provided via staticCompositionLocalOf), and MiuixPopupHost (placed in Scaffold's top z-slot) iterates those lists and renders each entry. Replicate with: (a) a registry — either an InheritedWidget (MiuixPopupRegistry) exposing 4 lists mirroring LocalPopupStates/LocalDialogStates/LocalRootPopupStates/LocalRootDialogStates, or a global ChangeNotifier singleton; (b) MiuixDialogLayout/MiuixPopupLayout as widgets returning SizedBox.shrink() that in initState/didUpdateWidget push+update a state and in dispose set showState=false (matching DisposableEffect onDispose); (c) a MiuixPopupHost widget that mounts a Stack of entries above content. `renderInRootScaffold` (default true) picks LocalRoot* list else Local* list — map to a root vs nested registry. `visible: MutableState<Boolean>` → ValueNotifier<bool>. When content==null: set visible=false and render nothing.

Z-INDEX: static counter nextZIndex starts at 1f, incremented per registered state (zIndex = nextZIndex++). Content drawn at zIndex; dim layer at zIndex-0.001; when no-dim, an invisible click-blocker at zIndex-0.002. Reset nextZIndex=1 only when both lists empty. In Flutter, order the Stack children by zIndex (sort dialogs then popups, each by zIndex). MiuixPopupHost iterates dialogStates THEN popupStates.

TRANSITION STATE MACHINE (per entry, replicate exactly): uses MutableTransitionState + pendingOpen + lastTarget. On showState=true: if animation NOT idle AND wasn't already opening (lastTarget false) → set pendingOpen=true (defer); else targetState=true. A second effect: when idle && pendingOpen → clear pendingOpen, targetState=true. On showState=false: pendingOpen=false, targetState=false. This debounces rapid toggles. In Flutter drive with an AnimationController.unbounded (or bounded 0..1); track isAnimating to gate pendingOpen. After exit completes (controller hits 0 / status dismissed), remove the state from the list AND (dialog only) invoke onDismissFinished — mirrors DisposableEffect onDispose that checks !showState.value.

EXACT ANIMATION SPECS (verbatim):
- Dialog dim ENTER: fadeIn tween(300ms, DecelerateEasing(1.5)). Dialog dim EXIT: fadeOut tween(250ms, DecelerateEasing(1.5)).
- Popup dim ENTER: fadeIn tween(300ms, SinOutEasing). Popup dim EXIT: fadeOut tween(150ms, SinOutEasing).
- Default dialog content ENTER, LARGE screen: fadeIn(spring dampingRatio=0.9, stiffness=438.6, visibilityThreshold=0.0001) + scaleIn(initialScale=0.8, SAME spring). SMALL screen: slideInVertically(initialOffsetY = full content height → slides up from bottom, spring dampingRatio=0.88, stiffness=450).
- Default dialog content EXIT, LARGE: fadeOut tween(200ms, DecelerateEasing(1.5)) + scaleOut(targetScale=0.8, tween(200ms, DecelerateEasing(1.5))). SMALL: slideOutVertically(targetOffsetY=full height, tween(200ms, DecelerateEasing(1.5))).
- Default popup content ENTER: fadeIn tween(200ms). EXIT: fadeOut tween(150ms).
Note enter uses SPRING but exit uses TWEEN for dialogs — controller must use SpringSimulation on forward and a curved duration tween on reverse. Build springs DIRECTLY as SpringDescription.withDampingRatio(mass:1, stiffness:438.6, ratio:0.9) and (mass:1, stiffness:450, ratio:0.88); do NOT route through folmeSpring (it derives stiffness from response — wrong here since stiffness is given). Equivalent response ≈ 0.300s (stiff 438.6) / 0.296s (stiff 450) if a response-based API is preferred. visibilityThreshold=0.0001 → SpringSimulation tolerance.

LARGE SCREEN: isLargeScreen = height>=480dp && width>=840dp (both). Uses windowInfo.containerDpSize → Flutter MediaQuery.of(context).size (width & height in logical px). effectiveLargeScreen = largeScreen && dialogState.enableAutoLargeScreen. Popups have NO large-screen variant.

DIM LAYER DRAWING: dialog dim draws drawRect(windowDimming.copy(alpha = windowDimming.alpha * dimAlpha)) where dimAlpha = dialogState.dimAlpha?.value.clamp(0,1) ?? 1 — supports a dynamic ValueNotifier<double> for interactive drag (bottom sheet) that bypasses the fade animation. Popup dim is just background(windowDimming), no dynamic alpha. In Flutter: ColoredBox/DecoratedBox with windowDimming, and for dialogs optionally windowDimming.withValues(alpha: windowDimming.a * dynamicAlpha).

SCRIM INPUT BLOCKING: both dim and no-dim branches wrap a fillMaxSize Box with pointerInput that consumes ALL pointer events every frame (blocks touches reaching content beneath) but does NOT dismiss on tap. Flutter equivalent: full-size AbsorbPointer, or opaque Listener/GestureDetector with HitTestBehavior.opaque. Dismissal is NOT via scrim tap here — only via back gesture (popups) or the content itself.

BACK HANDLER: ONLY PopupEntry has NavigationBackHandler (androidx.navigationevent) — isBackEnabled = enableBackHandler && (currentState||targetState), onBackCompleted sets showState=false. DialogEntry has NO back handler. Flutter: PopScope (Flutter 3.44) intercepting system back for the topmost enabled popup; predictive-back gesture animation is native, closest is PopScope + normal exit animation.

IME (dialog only): on dialog close, if WindowInsets.ime bottom>0 → keyboardController.hide(). Flutter: on dismiss, if MediaQuery.of(context).viewInsets.bottom>0 → FocusManager.instance.primaryFocus?.unfocus().

STATE FIELDS: DialogState{showState, zIndex, enterTransition?, exitTransition?, enableWindowDim=true, enableAutoLargeScreen=true, dimEnterTransition?, dimExitTransition?, dimAlpha:ValueNotifier<double>?, onDismissFinished?, content}. PopupState{showState, zIndex, enterTransition?, exitTransition?, enableWindowDim=true, enableBackHandler=true, dimEnterTransition?, dimExitTransition?, content}. Both entries wrap content in a fillMaxSize Box.

MOUNT POINT: MiuixPopupHost must sit above app content (Scaffold isn't ported yet). Mount it at app root (e.g. MaterialApp.builder wrapping child in a Stack with the host + registry) or in the future MiuixScaffold. Represent EnterTransition/ExitTransition as builder callbacks Widget Function(Animation<double> anim, Widget child) or a small spec class (fade/scale/slide flags + duration + curve/spring), since Compose EnterTransition/ExitTransition have no direct Flutter analogue.
MiuixPopupUtils.name: MiuixPopupUtils
MiuixPopupUtils.platformConcerns: 1) Predictive back / NavigationBackHandler (androidx.navigationevent): use Flutter PopScope (3.44 onPopInvokedWithResult) to intercept system back and dismiss the topmost enabled popup; only popups register it, dialogs do not. Predictive-back gesture scrubbing is native — closest is PopScope firing the standard exit animation. 2) Software keyboard: LocalSoftwareKeyboardController.hide() → FocusManager.instance.primaryFocus?.unfocus(); IME visibility via MediaQuery viewInsets.bottom. 3) Large-screen detection uses LocalWindowInfo.containerDpSize → MediaQuery.of(context).size (>=840w & >=480h). 4) Scrim pointer-consumption (every-frame consume) → AbsorbPointer / opaque Listener over full size; no ripple, no tap-dismiss. 5) staticCompositionLocalOf global registries → InheritedWidget or a global ChangeNotifier singleton. 6) Compose AnimatedVisibility with separate spring-enter/tween-exit specs has no 1:1 Flutter widget — drive manually via AnimationController (SpringSimulation forward, curved tween reverse) applying Opacity/Transform.scale/Transform.translate. 7) z-index stacking → ordered Stack children (or OverlayEntry order). No system blur involved (dim is a flat semi-transparent windowDimming color, fully replicable).

Tooltip.keyNotes:
DEFAULTS (verbatim, dp=logical px). SpacingBetweenTooltipAndAnchor=8. caretSize = width 16 x height 8. PlainTooltipMaxWidth=200; PlainTooltipCornerRadius=12; PlainTooltipInsideMargin = EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal:12, vertical:8). Plain container=colorScheme.onSecondaryVariant, content=colorScheme.secondaryVariant (inverse surface). Plain text uses textStyles.body2, maxLines:2, overflow ellipsis. RichTooltipMaxWidth=320; RichTooltipCornerRadius=16; RichTooltipInsideMargin=EdgeInsets.all(16). RichTooltipActionCornerRadius=8; RichTooltipActionInsideMargin=EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal:12, vertical:6). Rich colors: container=surfaceContainer, content=onSurfaceContainerVariant, title=onSurfaceContainer, action=primary. Rich body text=textStyles.body2; rich title=textStyles.subtitle. Rich layout = Column with 8dp vertical spacing between title/body/action; action wrapped in a Box aligned to End (right). Rich action button is a MiuixTextButton with transparent container, textColor=actionContentColor, minWidth:0, minHeight:0, cornerRadius:8, insideMargin=(h:12,v:6); on click invoke onActionClick then state.dismiss().

PERSISTENCE: plain default isPersistent=false (auto-dismiss after 1500ms via timer), rich default isPersistent=true (stays until outside tap / back / action). Default positioning = Below.

ANIMATIONS (enter/exit wrap the tooltip content; transformOrigin = center 0.5,0.5). Enter = fadeIn + scaleIn(from 0.9). fade enter = tween 200ms with Compose default easing (Curves.fastOutSlowIn). scale enter spring: dampingRatio=0.82, stiffness=362.5 -> folmeSpring(damping:0.82, response:0.33). Exit = fadeOut + scaleOut(to 0.9). fade exit = tween 150ms, Curves.fastOutSlowIn. scale exit spring (TooltipExitScaleSpec): DampingRatioNoBouncy=1.0, StiffnessMedium=1500 -> folmeSpring(damping:1.0, response:0.1622). Implement via AnimationController driving both a fade (opacity) and a scale; use spring for scale so an interrupted enter reverses smoothly (Kotlin note: must not hard-cut). Keep tooltip mounted while target=true OR still animating (mirror isVisible = targetState || !isIdle). NOTE: the ListPopupDefaults.AlphaEnter/Exit + FractionAnimationSpec are just these constants — inline them; ListPopup itself need not be ported first. MiuixPopupUtils is the only hard ordering dependency.

CARET: default caretShape=null => NO caret (Miuix caret-less is the default look). Caret drawn only when caretShape!=null AND positioning is Above or Below. caretOnTop = (positioning==Below). Draw in a CustomPainter behind the surface: anchorCenterX = anchorGlobalRect.left + anchorRect.width/2; selfX = tooltipGlobalRect.left; caretHalf = 8 (caretSize.width/2); cr = cornerRadius(px); centerX = (anchorCenterX - selfX).clamp(cr+8, tooltipWidth - cr - 8); caretHeight=8. If caretOnTop: triangle path (centerX,0)->(centerX-8,8)->(centerX+8,8) close. Else: (centerX,H)->(centerX-8,H-8)->(centerX+8,H-8) close. Fill with containerColor. When caret is drawn, add inner padding top=8 (if caretOnTop) or bottom=8 (else) so content clears the caret. The standalone TooltipCaretShape (for TooltipDefaults.caretShape()) is a downward-ish triangle: moveTo(w/2,0)->(0,h)->(w,h) close.

SURFACE STACK (outer->inner): Box widthIn(max: maxWidth) [measure self bounds] -> optional caret painter behind -> inner Box with padding(top/bottom for caret) -> dropShadow(RoundedRect cornerRadius, black@0.1, blur10) -> squircleBackground(containerColor, cornerRadius) -> padding(insideMargin) -> content. Use ShapeDecoration with MiuixSquircleBorder(cornerRadius:, enabled: cornerRadius>0) for the fill.

POSITION PROVIDER (flip + clamp), spacing default 8px. Cross-axis center: cx = anchor.left + (anchor.width - popupW)/2; cy = anchor.top + (anchor.height - popupH)/2. Resolve Start/End by text direction: Start->Left(LTR)/Right(RTL), End->Right(LTR)/Left(RTL). Below: below=anchor.bottom+spacing; above=anchor.top-popupH-spacing; y = (below+popupH <= winH || above<0) ? below : above; x=cx. Above: above=anchor.top-popupH-spacing; below=anchor.bottom+spacing; y = (above>=0 || below+popupH>winH) ? above : below; x=cx. Left: left=anchor.left-popupW-spacing; right=anchor.right+spacing; x = (left>=0 || right+popupW>winW) ? left : right; y=cy. Right: right=anchor.right+spacing; left=anchor.left-popupW-spacing; x = (right+popupW<=winW || left<0) ? right : left; y=cy. Final clamp: x=x.clamp(0, max(0, winW-popupW)); y=y.clamp(0, max(0, winH-popupH)).

GESTURES: touch/stylus long-press (500ms) -> show(UserInput priority) and swallow the up so anchor onTap doesn't also fire. Mouse enter -> show; mouse exit -> dismiss only if !isPersistent (lets cursor travel onto a persistent rich tooltip). enableUserInput=false disables both. State: transition target true/false; dismiss sets target=false (and cancels the job/timer if persistent). onDispose cancels timer/job. Only one tooltip visible globally at a time.
Tooltip.name: Tooltip
Tooltip.platformConcerns: Compose `Popup` + `PopupPositionProvider` -> Flutter `Overlay`+`OverlayEntry` (or `OverlayPortal`). No CompositedTransformFollower — the flip/clamp logic needs a custom positioning delegate that reads the anchor's window rect (via GlobalKey/RenderBox `localToGlobal`) and the tooltip's measured size, then computes offset exactly like TooltipPopupPositionProvider (see keyNotes). Mouse hover -> `MouseRegion(onEnter/onExit)`; onEnter shows, onExit dismisses only when NOT persistent. Long-press (touch/stylus) -> `GestureDetector(onLongPress:)` using Flutter's `kLongPressTimeout` (500ms); the Kotlin code consumes the following up-event so the anchor's own tap doesn't fire — replicate by having the long-press win the gesture arena / not forwarding the tap. Global single-tooltip behavior (MutatorMutex.GlobalMutatorMutex) -> a static/global reference to the active MiuixTooltipState; calling show() dismisses the previously active one. Auto-dismiss timeout (non-persistent) -> a `Timer` of BasicTooltipDefaults.TooltipDuration = 1500ms started on show, cancelled on manual dismiss; persistent tooltips skip the timer. focusable=true (rich) -> the overlay needs a full-screen tap-catcher barrier that dismisses on outside tap and lets cursor travel onto the tooltip; focusable=false (plain) -> no barrier, no outside-tap dismiss. Compose `dropShadow` (Shadow radius=10dp, black, alpha 0.1) -> `BoxShadow(color: Colors.black.withOpacity(0.1), blurRadius: 10)` on a RoundedRectangle; note the shadow uses a plain RoundedCornerShape(cornerRadius) while the fill uses squircleBackground — acceptable to shadow the squircle path directly. Semantics (liveRegion/paneTitle/onLongClick) -> Flutter `Semantics(liveRegion:true, label:..., onLongPress:...)`, low priority for fidelity.
